items.name: base
items.title: Manga base
items.description: Shared foundation for every mangacn item: ink/paper tokens mapped onto shadcn variables (dark mode is the negative) and one accent colour, --mg-accent (stamp red by default; presets via data-accent="indigo|pine|ochre"), which also drives --destructive. Screentone utilities (tone-10/20/35/50, tone-lines, tone-cross, tone-fade-r/l/t/b, tone-frame), on-tone (paper plate for labels over tones), knockout (outline for heavy SFX), speed-lines and focus-lines, tone-shadow (offset screentone, never a blur), ink-fill, focus-ink, border-ink, shape-burst, edge-jagged, mark-error, a reading-rtl: variant for manga reading order (data-reading="rtl"), a screentone veil for every shadcn overlay, and stepped 12 fps animations. Installed automatically as a dependency of every other item. Includes stepped keyframes for tabs, clicks, switches, dialogs and toasts; all motion stops with prefers-reduced-motion.
items.docs: mangacn base installed. Tones: tone-10|20|35|50, tone-lines, tone-cross, tone-fade-r|l|t|b, tone-frame; labels over tones go on an on-tone plate. Energy: speed-lines, focus-lines. Ink: border-ink, ink-fill, focus-ink, tone-shadow (positioned element). Accent: --mg-accent or data-accent="indigo|pine|ochre". Manga reading order: data-reading="rtl" + the reading-rtl: variant.

items.description: The JavaScript half of the mangacn grammar: punch() and withImpact() play the G4 impact on click or keyboard validation (data-impact for ~250 ms), <ImpactLines> draws the short speed lines outside the element, <FocusFlash> draws an optional halo of concentration lines around a window as it opens (G5, never full screen). items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: Manga-styled wrapper around your shadcn Button. Variants: default (ink flat), outline, tone (screentone band on the bottom third, label on paper), ghost, link (wavy underline that thickens on hover), destructive (accent colour, jagged edge), shout (burst shape for the one call to action on a page; its focus ring is a second burst). Sizes sm, default, lg, icon. Hover: a screentone shadow appears. Pressed: 2px offset and a negative that stays visible in dark mode. Disabled: dashed line, tone frame, label on paper. Adds loading (concentration lines turning in steps, aria-busy) and fullWidth. A click plays a three-frame impact (negative, recoil, settle) with short speed lines on both sides; the shout burst fidgets on hover.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: Manga-styled wrapper around your shadcn Select. The trigger is drawn like Input with a brush chevron that turns in two steps. The list is a case (3px ink line, tone shadow) with a notch toward the trigger, popping in over three frames. The highlighted option inverts to ink; the chosen option gets a brush check that draws itself. Group labels are underlined lettering; disabled options keep the label with a dashed underline. Adds SelectEmpty (a “…” mark) and SelectLoading (turning concentration lines).

items.name: speech-bubble
items.title: Speech Bubble
items.description: Manga speech bubble drawn in SVG at its real size and inscribed in its box, with real text inside. Variants: speech, thought (cloud), shout (spikes), whisper (dashed), narration (caption box), electronic (zigzag), wobbly (trembling). The tail points to top, bottom, start or end, aligned start/center/end, or none, and its room is reserved as margin; or pointAt={{ x, y }} (percent of the panel, in a Place) aims the tail at a point and lengthens it. Every length follows the font size, so on a Page the bubble scales with the page; there round bubbles square up a little to hold a block of text. align sets the text alignment, maxWidth the width limit (a percentage of the panel in a Place). BubbleGroup chains bubbles through a neck that hides both outlines.

items.name: panel
items.title: Panel
items.description: The manga page model. Page is a book page in a fixed format (pocket, magazine, square, or a free-height strip; spread for a double page) that keeps its proportions and scales as one block: lines, gutters, bubbles and sound effects are sized in container units of the page. A page is made of Tier (bands, height share, slant of the cut below) holding Panel (width share, slant of the cut after it) or Column (tiers inside a cell); the code order is the reading order, and reading="rtl" lays panels out right to left. Gutters between tiers are wider than between panels. Panel options: bleed, frameless, overflow, ink, inset (laid over the previous panel), shape straight | tilted | jagged | cloud | memory. Twelve templates (template prop): three-tiers, big-plus-two, l-shape, diagonal, four-koma, spread, grid-six, splash, inset, columns, shock, flashback; Panel children fill a template in order. Place puts any element in a panel in percent from an anchor (x="72%" y="12%" anchor="top-right") and keeps it inside the panel; SpeechBubble pointAt aims its tail. PanelArt shows a picture framed by a focal point and zoom, toned with TonedImage. The same page can be given as data (page prop, PageData JSON, same structure as the JSX; see page-geometry.ts). Under 480px the page folds into a vertical strip. pageGeometry(data) and onGeometry give each panel's box in reading order (percent of the page) for panel-by-panel readers. PanelGrid, the first CSS-grid layout (cols, rows, colSpan, rowSpan, cut, padding), stays for existing code and becomes Page when given a page, template, format or Tier children. PanelCaption is the narration box (corner or free).
items.docs: Import from "@/components/manga/panel". Tier, Panel and Column must be direct children of Page or Tier (not wrapped in your own components): the page reads them to lay out the page.

meta.tagline: A manga page: tiers, slanted cuts, templates, bubbles that aim.
meta.usage:
import { Page, Panel, PanelArt, Place, Tier } from "@/components/manga/panel"
import { SpeechBubble } from "@/components/manga/speech-bubble"

<Page format="pocket">
  <Tier height={2} slant={6}>
    <Panel bleed>
      <PanelArt src="/street.jpg" alt="A street at night" toned />
      <Place x="72%" y="12%" anchor="top-right">
        <SpeechBubble pointAt={{ x: "30%", y: "80%" }}>Over here!</SpeechBubble>
      </Place>
    </Panel>
  </Tier>
  <Tier>
    <Panel width={2} slant={-4} />
    <Panel shape="jagged" />
  </Tier>
</Page>

// or a template, or data
<Page template="big-plus-two"><Panel>…</Panel><Panel>…</Panel><Panel>…</Panel></Page>
<Page page={pageData} />

items.name: data-table
items.title: Data Table
items.description: A sortable, filterable, selectable table built on @tanstack/react-table and the mangacn Table. The table is a case with an ink header; sorted columns show a brush arrow (aria-sort); the hovered row gets its ink bar and selected rows a 6px bar. The toolbar has a filter field (filterColumn) and a column visibility menu (grouped, checkable items). Row selection uses the mangacn Checkbox, with a select-all in the header; pagination uses the mangacn Button. An empty filter result shows the "…" mark (TableEmpty). Props: columns, data, filterColumn?, pageSize?, onSelectionChange?(rows). Also exports selectColumn. On phones (table narrower than 640px) rows become cards: checkbox, title, badge, labelled lines; set `meta: { card: ... }` on a column to choose.
items.docs:
Import from "@/components/ui/manga/data-table". Column definitions use the TanStack v8 type ColumnDef<TData> (useReactTable with getCoreRowModel, getSortedRowModel, getFilteredRowModel and getPaginationRowModel). Every column with an accessorKey sorts unless enableSorting is false. Row ids are the index in data, so onSelectionChange returns the caller's own rows.

Phones: under `cardsBelow` (640px of table width) each row is a card. Per column, `meta: { card: "title" | "badge" | "line" | false }` sets its place (default: first column = title, others = lines).

meta.tagline: Sort, filter, select and page a list in an ink-lined table.
meta.usage:
import { DataTable } from "@/components/ui/manga/data-table"
import type { ColumnDef } from "@tanstack/react-table"

const columns: ColumnDef<Chapter>[] = [
  { accessorKey: "title", header: "Chapter" },
  { accessorKey: "pages", header: "Pages" },
]

<DataTable columns={columns} data={chapters} filterColumn="title" pageSize={10} onSelectionChange={(rows) => setPicked(rows)} />

items.name: carousel
items.title: Carousel
items.description: Manga-styled wrapper around your shadcn Carousel (embla). Every slide is a panel: its content gets a 2px ink frame on paper (ink-case-inner). Previous / Next are the kit outline icon button with a brush arrow: the tone shadow appears on hover, pressed is a negative with impact lines, focus is the ink / paper / ink ring, disabled is dashed with a tone frame. Under 640px they grow to 44px and sit inside the carousel width, in a row under the slides (stock places them 48px outside). Adds CarouselDots, a mangacn addition built on useCarousel: square dots, the current one an ink flat that sweeps in, 24px hit areas (44px under 640px). Manga reading order: under data-reading="rtl" (or opts.direction "rtl", or dir="rtl") embla runs right to left, slides flow right to left, the arrows and arrow keys follow; text stays left to right. Vertical orientation puts the buttons above and below and uses the up / down keys.

The carousel follows the page's manga reading order (data-reading="rtl") and writing direction (dir="rtl") by itself; opts.direction overrides it. From 640px the buttons sit 48px outside the slides, as in shadcn: leave room around the carousel (sm:px-12). Vertical: give CarouselContent a height and leave room above and below for the buttons (py-14). Put one element in each CarouselItem: it becomes the panel.

items.description: A speech or thought bubble (the kit SpeechBubble) that first shows three small ink squares rising one after another at 12 fps (waiting), then writes its text a few characters per frame with a stepped block caret. items.name: page-reader
items.title: Page Reader
items.description: A manga read page by page from a list of images ({ src, alt, width, height }). One page or two-page spreads (auto: spreads when the stage is wide and landscape; the cover stands alone), manga order (right to left: the next page is on the left, a spread puts the lower page on the right) or western order. Turn with the page edges (invisible zones that show a paper plate with a brush arrow on hover), the arrow keys (following the order), Page Up / Down, Home / End, a swipe (the page follows the finger with no steps, then turns or snaps back; it resists at both ends) or the toolbar. Fit: whole page, width (scrolls down) or height. Background: paper, ink or tone. Zoom 100–300 % with buttons, + / - / 0 or a double click at a point, then drag to pan. Full screen asks the browser (Fullscreen API on the document) and falls back to a fixed immersive mode (iOS Safari); Escape leaves. Pages around the current one are fetched ahead (preload), and a page known to be loaded shows at once. Each page is a ReaderPage (ink frame, loading panel, jagged error panel with Retry, a paper mat in dark mode). A turned page slides in from the side it comes from in three steps. An optional end view after the last page holds a ChapterEnd. The toolbar has a ReadingProgress with a page counter and a slot for your own buttons (settings, thumbnails). Controlled or not (page / onPageChange). Built at 375 px first: 44 px controls, two toolbar rows. PageReader also takes pages of the page model ({ page: PageData }), drawn by Page with real lettering; scans and data pages can be mixed.

items.name: guided-view
items.title: Guided View
items.description: A manga read panel by panel, made for phones: the screen zooms from one panel to the next. It reads the panel geometry of the page model (pageGeometry: every panel's box in reading order, insets included), so a page written as PageData is drawn by Page and guided without any extra data; scans work too, with the box of each panel in percent of the page. The page is drawn once at a fixed width and a camera fits the current panel in the stage, moving in four steps (333 ms); the panels around it hide under a paper veil with wide dots that steps aside while the camera travels. A new page slides in from the side it comes from. Next and previous by tapping the page edges (on hover a paper plate with a brush arrow), the arrow keys following the reading order, Space, Page Up / Down, Home / End, a swipe (the page follows the finger, then turns or snaps back) or the toolbar. Whole page shows the page with every panel as a target (the current one framed, hover thickens a panel's line). A ReadingProgress counts the panels; a live region reads each panel's label. Optional end view (e.g. a ChapterEnd) and a slot for your buttons. Reduced motion: the camera jumps.

items.name: chapter-end
items.title: Chapter End
items.description: The end card of a chapter: a 3px panel whose concentration lines surround a central paper plate, with the chapter line, the big SFX word (To be continued, or The end for a finished series) and a brush arrow in the reading direction (a check at the end of a series). Under it, the next chapter as a full-width button with its number, title and optional cover, or, when it is not out yet, the date in a stamp; then any actions the reader wants (back to the series, comments). Under the manga reading order (data-reading="rtl") the arrow points left. The panel pops in once.

Reading order follows the nearest data-reading attribute (rtl for manga, ltr for western): the arrow turns and the arrow sits before the word. items.title: Shelf
items.description: Manga volumes standing spine out on a shelf. Pulling a volume (click, Enter) turns its spine into an ink flat raised by 16px in two steps and drops its VolumeCard in under the shelf (cover, status, reading progress) with Open and Put back buttons. Arrows move along the row, Home / End, Escape puts the volume back and returns the focus to its spine. items.name: release-calendar
items.title: Release Calendar
items.description: Releases by day of the week. On a narrow screen a day strip drawn like boxed tabs (one frame split into seven cells, the selected day an ink flat, today marked with a corner triangle) shows the releases of one day below it, with arrow, Home and End keys. From a container of 56 rem up, seven columns show every day at once, today's header an ink flat. Each release is a case with its cover, time, title and chapter, a NEW burst or a Break stamp; rows with an href are links, rows with onSelect are buttons, both with the hover lift, the ink focus ring and the pressed offset. A day without releases shows a short line in a fine frame.
items.docs: Import from "@/components/manga/release-calendar". Weekdays are numbers, Monday first (0 = Monday, 6 = Sunday). The day strip is the narrow layout and the columns are the wide one, switched by the width of the component's container (container query, 56 rem); force one with layout="strip" or layout="columns". Pass today to fix the marked day, otherwise it is computed from the current date. Day labels are passed as seven short strings, Monday first. Wide columns need about 56 rem: put the component in a horizontal scroll area below that width.

meta.tagline: A week of releases: a day strip on phones, seven columns on wide screens.

import { ReleaseCalendar, type Release } from "@/components/manga/release-calendar"

const releases: Release[] = [

  { id: "2", day: 2, title: "Paper Comet", chapter: "Ch. 18", time: "18:00", status: "break" },
]

items.description: A wipe that sweeps the screen (or a container) between two sections or pages, in steps: four frames to cover, a hold, four frames to uncover, at 12 fps, swapping the scene while the screen is covered. Variants: ink (an ink flat), tone (a 50% screentone on paper edged with ink lines), panels (four ink panels with paper gutters dropped one per frame). The overlay is aria-hidden and catches clicks while it plays; with reduced motion the scene is swapped at once.

items.description: Furigana: small readings over (or under, or beside in vertical text) the characters they read, in native <ruby> / <rt> markup with <rp> fallbacks so the text copies, wraps and reads aloud. CSS only, no JavaScript.

items.name: manga-reader
items.title: Manga Reader
items.description: A webtoon-style chapter reader made only with mangacn: a top bar with the series and chapter, a Full screen toggle (pressed button) and a Chapters button opening a Sheet headed by a VolumeCard of the current volume (drawn SVG cover, ongoing status, chapters read / out as a running-line bar) above the chapter list (the current chapter is an ink flat, read chapters carry a brush check), a reading-order switch of pressed buttons (Manga RTL / Western LTR) that sets data-reading on the root and flips the previous / next chapter buttons, a ReadingProgress bar with a "Page 3 / 9" counter fed by the strip, a ReaderStrip of nine drawn pages (lazy images, END panel), previous / next chapter buttons and a comments strip (Message, Bubble, ReactionPicker, Input). From @md/main up, on screens at least 36rem tall, the reader fills a 46rem frame that scrolls inside and the progress bar sticks to the top of the frame and measures it; on phones it follows the page and the progress bar sticks to the bottom edge. Full screen makes the reader root fixed inset-0 with its own scroll (data-fullscreen="immersive", also the fallback when the Fullscreen API is missing or refused, e.g. iOS Safari) and asks the browser for full screen on the document element (data-fullscreen="native"), so the Sheet still opens above it; Escape or the button leaves. Works in light, dark, any accent and at phone width.

items.description: The site of a manga author, end to end, made only with mangacn: a header with the author's name and a breadcrumb, then three screens that lead to each other. items.description: The sign-in screen of the mangacn auth flow, made only with the kit. A manga Panel: the reader drawn whole in SVG (ink lines, paper fills, a screentone jacket, an open volume), focus SpeedLines around her, a SpeechBubble ('Welcome back! From 48rem of container width the panel stands full height on the start side of the form; narrower, it sits above the form in 4:3 with the character whole. items.title: Verify code
items.description: The one-time code screen of a manga auth flow, made only with mangacn. A manga Panel shows a reader drawn whole in SVG (ink lines, paper fills, a screentone jacket) holding the email that just arrived, focus SpeedLines around her, 'ピコン' Sfx lettering and a SpeechBubble that reacts: 'Check your inbox!', a shout bubble 'Huh?!' on error, 'Yes!' on success. From 48rem of container width the panel sits on the start side at the full height of the form; under it the panel is a 4:3 picture above the form. The form, in a case (G1) when there is room: InputOTP with one group of 6 digits (fits 360px), a Button with its loading state, a resend link after a 30 s countdown (only the end and the resend are announced) and 'Use another email'. Fewer than six digits shows a Field error; the wrong code 000000 shows the G8 error box (accent fill, edge-jagged, '!' mark, shake, role=alert) and the InputOTP invalid look, focus back in the code; any other full code loads, then the success Stamp lands with the next action. The purpose prop (sign-in, sign-up, reset) changes the copy, the stamp ('Welcome back!', 'Welcome!', 'Verified!') and the next screen. Links call onNavigate and never navigate by themselves. One column on phones with 44px touch targets; container queries widen it. Works in light, dark, any accent and with Radix or Base UI.
